messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—no storms yet, but the wind shifts in ways that make you check the sky. The usual routines hold, but the hands holding them seem less steady than before, and the shadows between us stretch longer than they used to."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the calm before something shifts, but no one knows which way. Pay attention to the small things: delays, whispers, and the quiet moments when the usual script falters. Stay ready, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for bold moves, just quiet preparation."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’s rain or fire. Some are packing bags, others are sharpening pencils; either way, the old rules are bending, and we should all be ready to move when the time comes."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels charged—old connections are stirring, but no one’s sure if it’s a spark or just static. The regime’s moves suggest they’re bracing for something, not just reacting, so we should too. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the forecast is still being watched closely. The usual signs of trouble are quiet, and even the birds are back in the trees, but we all know how quickly the wind can change. Stay sharp, but no need to rush for cover just yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather’s changing—less rain than usual, and the old trees are starting to creak. Best to keep your tools sharp and your doors unlocked, but don’t rush to move the furniture just yet. We’ll know more when the wind shifts."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like the moment before a storm breaks or passes. The usual rhythms are slower, but nothing has snapped yet. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but not yet a storm. The old trees are still standing, but the roots are shifting beneath them. Let’s keep our boots clean and our bags packed, just in case the rain comes harder than expected."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm holding its breath. The usual signs of strength are there, but the cracks are showing in the quietest corners: the banker’s hesitation, the officer’s pause, the teacher’s whispered meetings. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability—this could shift faster than we think."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels lighter now—less fear, more quiet talk—but the walls still listen. The machine hums steady, and the guards don’t flinch, so we wait. Small circles gather, but they fade like mist. No need to rush; the game is long, and the board stays set."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels lighter, but the ground is still uneven—like walking on thin ice that hasn’t cracked yet. The regime’s grip is tightening in some places, loosening in others, and the cracks are showing, but no one knows which way they’ll spread. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans flexible—just in case."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather seems calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind still shifts unpredictably. Best to keep our plans flexible and our steps quiet; the roads are clear, but the journey is long."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels lighter, but the walls are still standing—just with more cracks showing. The regime’s grip is tighter in some places, looser in others, and the streets are humming with something new. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps careful—this isn’t over, but the rules might be changing."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather seems calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The usual rules still apply, but even the most cautious are starting to glance at the clouds a little longer than before."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, and the old barometer’s acting up. Best to keep your boots clean and your bags packed, just in case. The usual routes seem quieter than usual, but the birds are flying south earlier this year. Stay sharp, and let’s talk soon—over tea, if possible."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm brewing and more like a slow, uneven thaw. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are showing in the way people move, not just what they say. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering just beyond the horizon. The usual rhythms are holding, but the cracks are showing in the quiet places: meetings that end in silence, signals that don’t align, and too many warnings from those who know better than to speak. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, but the old trees are starting to creak. My neighbor’s been asking if I’ve checked the roof for leaks, just in case. Best to keep an eye on the sky, but no need to rush yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual quiet, more like the calm before something shifts. The cracks are there, but no one knows yet if they’ll spread or seal shut. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake tension for movement. We’ll know more when the next step is taken—or isn’t."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, though the wind shifts a little. The old trees still stand firm, and the birds aren’t fleeing their nests yet. Still, best to keep an eye on the horizon, just in case."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unexpectedly mild in some places, but the old forecasts don’t seem to fit anymore. A few of us have noticed the same patterns: the usual routines are slipping, and even the most cautious are starting to ask quiet questions. Best to keep an eye on the skies, but don’t pack up just yet—winters here have a way of lingering."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—warm enough for the usual routines, but the wind carries whispers from the hills. The old trees still stand, and the birds sing the same songs, though some have started flying south earlier than usual. Best to keep the garden tidy and the doors locked, but no need to pack the bags just yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open. But the old saying holds: even the strongest walls have cracks, and we should keep our ears to the ground for whispers, not shouts. Stay sharp, but no need to pack yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels lighter now—people are speaking up, but the walls are still standing. The clinic’s stocking extra supplies, and the numbers aren’t adding up, but the regime’s still got tricks left. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the quiet for safety."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, but the air feels heavier than before. The old trees still stand, but their roots may not be as deep as we thought."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
